<!-- Title: type(slug): a plain sentence saying what is now true. No file or function names.
Types: feat(<slug>) · fix(<slug>) or fix · docs · plan · contract · revert (also refactor, perf, test, chore, style).
The full convention, with an example: specs/context/pull-requests.md. Write for a curious reader who does not program. -->

Closes #<!-- the feature's issue -->

## In plain words
<!-- Two or three sentences: what is different now, for someone who has never seen the code. -->

## Why
<!-- The main section. The question that forced a choice · what we chose and the reason · what we turned down and
why · who decided (quote Eric with the date, or link the decision file). -->

## What changed
<!-- Short list. Plain words first, then the path in backticks. -->

## See it
<!-- Required if this changes a drawing, a score, a true border, a prompt or the page: preview, contact sheet or
screenshot, embedded by raw URL at the latest commit, with one sentence on what to look at. Otherwise: "Nothing to see." -->

## Does any score change?
<!-- "No." or a before/after table and the reason. A change to a public score waits for Eric. -->

## Sources
<!-- If data or a historical fact enters the repo: link, licence, what was taken, every edit, each judgment call.
Otherwise delete this section. -->

## Cost
<!-- If models were called: calls, dollars, running total against the cap. Otherwise delete this section. -->

## Checks
<!-- Each command and the last lines it printed. A fix: the failing line on origin/main, then the passing one.
- Spec validation:
- Verify: the line verify.py printed, or `not verified` and why
- CI on this exact revision:
- Done note `changes/<slug>.md` written last (feat PRs only) -->

## Not done, not sure
<!-- Merged is not the same as checked by a person. List anything skipped, untested or unknown. -->
